title: The light bulb that has burned since 1901
hook: A light bulb in a California fire station has been glowing since 1901.
peek: In a fire station in Livermore, California, a hand-blown bulb has been shining since 1901, with only a few short breaks. Today it gives off about as much light as a night light, and a webcam lets anyone check that it is still on.
lede: The Centennial Light hangs from the ceiling of Fire Station 6 in Livermore, California. It was hand-blown by the Shelby Electric Company in Ohio and first switched on in 1901. It has glowed almost without a break ever since, and Guinness World Records lists it as the longest-lasting light bulb. In 2015 it passed one million hours.

bullets.text: The bulb has a carbon filament and now runs at only about 4 watts, giving a soft glow like a night light. Running it so gently, and almost never switching it off, is a big part of why it has lasted.
When the fire department moved to a new station in 1976, the bulb was unplugged for about 22 minutes and driven across town with a fire engine escort. It lit up again in its new home.

Volunteers set up a webcam so anyone can watch the bulb online. In 2013 the camera showed it dark and fans feared it had gone out for good, but the fault was a failed power supply. About nine and a half hours later, the bulb shone again.
A committee of local volunteers looks after the bulb and its history. They have thrown parties for its 100th birthday in 2001 and for its millionth hour of light in 2015.
